tools.name: heliyos_records_list
tools.title: List records
tools.description: Lists records of one object (companies, people, deals, or a custom object) in the Heliyos workspace, newest first. Use it to browse or filter records; use heliyos_records_lookup to find a record by name and heliyos_records_get for one record. Filter with `search` (free text) and `filters` (field conditions joined by `match`); order with `sort`. Returns a table of id, name and key fields plus structuredContent {records:[{id, object_type, name, fields}], next_cursor}. When next_cursor is present, call again with `cursor` set to it for the next page. Record ids feed heliyos_records_get, _update and _delete.

object_type.description: Which object: "company", "person", "deal", or "custom" (custom objects also need schema_id).

schema_id.description: Object schema id. Required when object_type is "custom"; the error lists the available ones.

search.description: Plain words matched across the record's text fields. Symbols such as + ( ) [ ] * ? can cause an error.

filters.description: Field conditions, for example [{field:"stage", operator:"equals", value:"Won"}]. Joined by `match`.

field.description: Field key, for example stage or domain. createdAt, updatedAt and isAgentAssigned also work.

operator.description: How to compare: contains, notContains, startsWith, endsWith (text); equals, notEquals; empty, notEmpty (no value); greaterThan, greaterThanOrEqual, lessThan, lessThanOrEqual (numbers); after, before (dates).

value.description: Value to compare with. Text operators (contains, notContains, startsWith, endsWith) need text; a comma in a contains value matches any of the parts. Omit for empty and notEmpty. Dates as ISO 8601.

match.description: "all" (default): a record must meet every filter condition. "any": at least one condition.

sort.description: Sort order. Omit for newest updated first. With a sort, next_cursor is a page cursor from this tool; pass it back unchanged.

field.description: Field key to sort by (from heliyos_objects_get), or createdAt / updatedAt.

cursor.description: next_cursor from the previous page, with the same limit. Omit for the first page.

response_format.description: "concise" (default) returns the name and key fields; "detailed" returns every field and linked records.

relationships.description: Linked records; only with response_format detailed.

tools.name: heliyos_records_get
tools.title: Get a record
tools.description: Fetches one record (a company, person, deal, or custom object row) by id. Use it after heliyos_records_list or heliyos_records_lookup gives you an id. "concise" returns the name, key fields and a count of linked records; "detailed" returns every field, the linked records (for example a person's company or a company's deals) with their ids, and created and updated times. Returns structuredContent {record:{id, object_type, schema_id, name, fields, relationships}}.

response_format.description: "concise" (default) returns the name and key fields; "detailed" returns every field and linked records.

relationships.description: Linked records; only with response_format detailed.

tools.name: heliyos_records_create
tools.title: Create a record
tools.description: Creates one record (a company, person, deal, or custom object row) with the given field values. Check first with heliyos_records_lookup that the record does not already exist; calling this twice creates two records. Creating a company can start automatic enrichment, which uses credits when automatic enrichment is on (Settings, Autopilot). Returns the new record's id and key fields as structuredContent {record}.

object_type.description: Which object: "company", "person", "deal", or "custom" (custom objects also need schema_id).

schema_id.description: Object schema id. Required when object_type is "custom"; the error lists the available ones.

fields.description: Field values keyed by the object's field keys (for example company_name, domain, people_name, email, deal_name, stage). Unknown keys are rejected with the list of valid keys. `relationships` takes an array of record ids to link to this record (for example a person's company); linking adds to the existing links, and updates never remove links.

relationships.description: Linked records; only with response_format detailed.

tools.name: heliyos_records_update
tools.title: Update a record
tools.description: Updates some fields of one record by id; fields you leave out keep their values. Set a field to null to clear it. Field keys are checked against the record's object first, and unknown keys are rejected with the valid ones. `relationships` adds links and never removes existing ones. Get the id from heliyos_records_list or heliyos_records_lookup. Returns the changed fields and the record's key fields as structuredContent {record}.

fields.description: Field values keyed by the object's field keys (for example company_name, domain, people_name, email, deal_name, stage). Unknown keys are rejected with the list of valid keys. `relationships` takes an array of record ids to link to this record (for example a person's company); linking adds to the existing links, and updates never remove links.

relationships.description: Linked records; only with response_format detailed.

tools.name: heliyos_records_delete
tools.title: Delete records
tools.description: Permanently deletes up to 100 records of one object by id. This cannot be undone: confirm with the user first. All ids must belong to the given object_type; the API ignores ids from other objects and does not confirm a count. Returns structuredContent {deleted_count (ids sent), record_ids}.

object_type.description: Which object: "company", "person", "deal", or "custom" (custom objects also need schema_id).

schema_id.description: Object schema id. Required when object_type is "custom"; the error lists the available ones.

items.description: each record_ids entry: a 24-character hex id.

record_ids.description: Ids of the records to delete, 1 to 100.

deleted_count.description: Number of distinct ids sent; the API does not confirm the count.

tools.name: heliyos_records_lookup
tools.title: Find records by name
tools.description: Finds records of one object whose name contains `query` (case-insensitive; exact and prefix matches rank first), or whose secondary value does (the first of domain, email, job title or stage that the object has). Use it to turn a name the user mentions into a record id. It searches the 2000 most recently updated records; for older ones use heliyos_records_list with search. Returns structuredContent {matches:[{id, name, secondary}], total_matches}.

object_type.description: Which object: "company", "person", "deal", or "custom" (custom objects also need schema_id).

schema_id.description: Object schema id. Required when object_type is "custom"; the error lists the available ones.

query.description: Name or part of a name, for example "acme".

limit.description: Maximum matches to return, 1 to 100. Default 20.

response_format.description: "concise" (default) returns the name and key fields; "detailed" returns every field and linked records.

tools.name: heliyos_records_enrich
tools.title: Enrich a person
tools.description: Experimental. Looks up public profile data for one person record (job title, LinkedIn and similar) and writes it to the record. Only person records can be enriched; companies are enriched automatically when watched. Each call uses 20 credits and fails when fewer remain, so confirm with the user first. Returns the updated record's key fields as structuredContent {record}.

relationships.description: Linked records; only with response_format detailed.

tools.name: heliyos_organization_get
tools.title: Get the workspace
tools.description: Returns the Heliyos workspace this API key belongs to: its id and name, billing status, active plan, member count, how many companies, people and deals it holds, and how many companies are watched out of the plan's limit. Call it first to orient yourself. Use heliyos_objects_list for the objects and their schema ids, heliyos_usage_get for credit usage. Returns structuredContent {organization}.

plan.description: Active plan name; absent when the workspace has no active plan.

watchers_limit.description: Watched-company limit of the active plan.

tools.name: heliyos_objects_list
tools.title: List objects
tools.description: Lists the workspace's objects (record types): companies, people, deals and any custom objects, with each one's schema_id, object_type, record count and number of fields. Use it to learn which object_type and schema_id to pass to the heliyos_records_* tools (custom objects need schema_id), then heliyos_objects_get for an object's field keys. Returns every object in one page (a workspace has a handful), as structuredContent {objects}.

response_format.description: "concise" (default) returns one line per object; "detailed" returns each object's field keys too.

stored_type.description: The platform's own objectType value (for example people, deals).

fields.description: Detailed only: the object's field keys in order.

tools.name: heliyos_objects_get
tools.title: Get an object's fields
tools.description: Returns one object's fields: each field key (what heliyos_records_create, _update and _list filters take), its label and type, and which are required. "detailed" adds the allowed values of select fields, hidden and AI-filled flags, and the target object of relationship fields. Pick the object with object_type (company, person, deal, or custom with schema_id from heliyos_objects_list). Each field's field_id feeds heliyos_fields_update and heliyos_fields_delete; heliyos_fields_create adds one. Returns structuredContent {object:{schema_id, name, fields:[{key, field_id, type, ...}]}}.

object_type.description: Which object: "company", "person", "deal", or "custom" (custom objects also need schema_id).

schema_id.description: Object schema id. Required when object_type is "custom"; the error lists the available ones.

response_format.description: "concise" (default) returns each field's key, label and type; "detailed" returns select options and field flags too.

stored_type.description: The platform's own objectType value (for example people, deals).

key.description: The field key to use in record `fields` and filters.

field_id.description: The field's id, for heliyos_fields_update and heliyos_fields_delete.

type.description: text, number, currency, date, timestamp, select, multiSelect, url, email, phone, user, relationship, ...

hidden.description: Detailed only: hidden in the web app's tables.

options.description: Detailed only: allowed values of a select or multiSelect field.

ai_enabled.description: Detailed only: the field is filled by an AI prompt.

relationship_schema_id.description: Detailed only: the object a relationship field links to.

tools.name: heliyos_objects_create
tools.title: Create a custom object
tools.description: Experimental. Creates a custom object (a new record type, for example Partners or Investors). The platform gives it one text field named after the object and one empty record. Calling it twice creates two objects, so check heliyos_objects_list first. Returns structuredContent {object:{schema_id, name}}; pass that schema_id with object_type "custom" to the records tools, and add fields with heliyos_fields_create.

description.description: What the object holds, shown in the web app.

icon.description: Web app icon name. Default PiFile02AiStroke.

tools.name: heliyos_objects_update
tools.title: Rename or describe an object
tools.description: Experimental. Changes an object's name, description or icon by schema_id. Fields are not changed here. Returns structuredContent {object:{schema_id, name}}.

description.description: New description; an empty string clears it.

tools.name: heliyos_objects_delete
tools.title: Delete a custom object
tools.description: Experimental. Permanently deletes a custom object AND every record in it. This cannot be undone: confirm with the user first, naming the object and its record count (heliyos_objects_list). Only custom objects can be deleted; built-in objects (companies, people, deals) are refused, and so is any object whose type cannot be read. Returns structuredContent {schema_id, deleted}.

tools.name: heliyos_fields_create
tools.title: Add a field to an object
tools.description: Adds one field (column) to an object: companies, people, deals or a custom object (object_type, plus schema_id for custom). Give it a label and a type; select and multiSelect need `options`; `ai_prompt` makes it an AI column. The field key (what record `fields` and filters use) is derived from the label unless `key` is given, and must be new on the object. Relationship fields are created in the Heliyos web app. Calling this twice with the same key fails. Returns structuredContent {field:{field_id, key, label, type}}.

object_type.description: Which object: "company", "person", "deal", or "custom" (custom objects also need schema_id).

schema_id.description: Object schema id. Required when object_type is "custom"; the error lists the available ones.

key.description: Field key, for example contract_value. Derived from the label when omitted.

type.description: One of text, richText, number, currency, rating, checkbox, date, timestamp, select, multiSelect, url, email, phone, user, image, file.

description.description: What the field holds; shown in the web app and read by the workers.

options.description: Allowed values of a select or multiSelect field, unique.

required.description: Records must have a value. Default false.

hidden.description: Hidden from the web app's tables by default. Default false.

visibility.description: "organization" (default): every member sees it; "private": only owners and admins.

ai_prompt.description: Makes this an AI column: the workers fill it from this prompt (text, richText, number, date, select, multiSelect or checkbox only). Filling existing records is started from the Heliyos web app and uses credits.

key.description: The key to use in record `fields` and list filters.

tools.name: heliyos_fields_update
tools.title: Change a field
tools.description: Changes one field of an object by field_id (from heliyos_objects_get): its label, description, options, required or hidden flag, AI prompt, or type. What you leave out is kept. `options` REPLACES the allowed values, and records holding a removed value keep it as stale text. A type change is refused by the platform when existing values do not fit the new type. The field key never changes. Returns structuredContent {field}.

object_type.description: Which object: "company", "person", "deal", or "custom" (custom objects also need schema_id).

schema_id.description: Object schema id. Required when object_type is "custom"; the error lists the available ones.

description.description: What the field holds; shown in the web app and read by the workers.

type.description: New type; values must fit it.

options.description: Allowed values of a select or multiSelect field, unique.

required.description: true: records must have a value.

hidden.description: true: hidden from the web app's tables by default.

ai_prompt.description: Makes this an AI column: the workers fill it from this prompt (text, richText, number, date, select, multiSelect or checkbox only). Filling existing records is started from the Heliyos web app and uses credits.

key.description: The key to use in record `fields` and list filters.

tools.name: heliyos_fields_delete
tools.title: Delete a field
tools.description: Permanently deletes one field of an object by field_id (from heliyos_objects_get) AND its value on every record. This cannot be undone: confirm with the user first, naming the field and the object. Built-in required fields (for example a company's name) are refused by the platform. Returns structuredContent {field_id, key, deleted}.

object_type.description: Which object: "company", "person", "deal", or "custom" (custom objects also need schema_id).

schema_id.description: Object schema id. Required when object_type is "custom"; the error lists the available ones.

tools.name: heliyos_records_timeline
tools.title: Read a record's timeline
tools.description: Returns the AI-written timeline of one record (company, person or deal): the record's current relationship summary and dated entries describing what happened (emails, meetings, deal moves), newest first. Use it to brief yourself on an account before acting. For the raw audit trail of field changes use heliyos_records_events; for the emails and meetings themselves use heliyos_interactions_list. Returns structuredContent {record_id, summary, entries, next_cursor}.

cursor.description: next_cursor from the previous page, with the same limit. Omit for the first page.

response_format.description: "concise" (default) returns each entry cut at 300 characters; "detailed" returns full entry text.

tools.name: heliyos_records_events
tools.title: Read a record's change history
tools.description: Returns the audit trail of one record: who changed what and when (people and workers), newest first, each with a one-line change summary. Filter by operation type, event type, date range or text. "detailed" adds the paths of the changed fields. Use heliyos_records_timeline instead for a narrative of the relationship. Returns structuredContent {events:[{id, at, operation_type, actor, change_summary}], next_cursor}.

operation_types.description: Only these operations: CREATE, UPDATE, DELETE.

event_types.description: Only these event types: AUDIT (field changes), INTERACTION (emails, meetings), ENRICHMENT.

since.description: since as an ISO 8601 date (2026-03-01) or date-time (2026-03-01T09:00:00Z).

until.description: Only events at or before this date; a date alone includes that whole day (UTC).

search.description: Plain words matched against the change summaries. Symbols such as + ( ) [ ] * ? can cause an error.

cursor.description: next_cursor from the previous page, with the same limit. Omit for the first page.

response_format.description: "concise" (default) returns one line per change; "detailed" returns the changed field paths too.

actor.description: Who made the change (a person's or worker's name).

changed_fields.description: Detailed only: paths whose value changed.

tools.name: heliyos_interactions_list
tools.title: List emails and meetings
tools.description: Lists synced emails and meetings, newest first, optionally only those linked to one record (record_id) or of one channel. Each has its subject or title, time, AI summary and the records it is linked to. "detailed" adds participants and next steps; heliyos_interactions_get returns one with its full summary. Order with `sort`. Returns structuredContent {interactions:[{id, channel, title, at, summary, record_ids}], next_cursor}.

record_id.description: Only interactions linked to this record (company, person or deal).

search.description: Plain words matched against subjects, titles and summaries. Symbols such as + ( ) [ ] * ? can cause an error.

sort.description: Sort order. Omit for newest first. With a sort, next_cursor is a page cursor from this tool; pass it back unchanged.

field.description: last_message (newest email thread message), start_time (meeting start) or created_at (when it was synced).

cursor.description: next_cursor from the previous page, with the same limit. Omit for the first page.

response_format.description: "concise" (default) returns subject, time and a summary cut at 300 characters; "detailed" returns the full summary, participants and next steps.

at.description: Last message time (email) or start time (meeting).

record_ids.description: Records this interaction is linked to.

tools.name: heliyos_interactions_get
tools.title: Get an email or meeting
tools.description: Fetches one synced email thread or meeting by id (from heliyos_interactions_list or heliyos_records_timeline): subject or title, time, the AI summary, sentiment, the records it is linked to, participants and next steps. "concise" cuts the summary; "detailed" returns all of it. Returns structuredContent {interaction}.

response_format.description: "concise" (default) returns the summary cut at 300 characters; "detailed" returns the full summary, participants and next steps.

at.description: Last message time (email) or start time (meeting).

record_ids.description: Records this interaction is linked to.

tools.name: heliyos_notes_list
tools.title: List notes
tools.description: Lists notes, newest first, optionally only those linked to one record (record_id) or matching text in the title or body. Each note shows its id, title, a short preview and the records it is linked to. Use heliyos_notes_get for the full text. Returns structuredContent {notes:[{id, title, content, links}], next_cursor}.

record_id.description: Only notes linked to this record.

search.description: Plain words matched against note titles and bodies. Symbols such as + ( ) [ ] * ? can cause an error.

cursor.description: next_cursor from the previous page, with the same limit. Omit for the first page.

response_format.description: "concise" (default) returns a 200-character preview; "detailed" returns each note's full text and times.

content.description: Concise: cut (list: 200, get: 1500 characters); detailed: complete.

object_type.description: company, person, deal, custom, or a non-record target such as task or interaction.

tools.name: heliyos_notes_get
tools.title: Get a note
tools.description: Fetches one note by id with its title, text and linked records. "concise" cuts the text at 1500 characters; "detailed" returns all of it plus created and updated times. Returns structuredContent {note}.

response_format.description: "concise" (default) returns the text cut at 1500 characters; "detailed" returns the full text and times.

content.description: Concise: cut (list: 200, get: 1500 characters); detailed: complete.

object_type.description: company, person, deal, custom, or a non-record target such as task or interaction.

tools.name: heliyos_notes_create
tools.title: Create a note
tools.description: Creates a note, optionally linked to records (a company, person or deal) so it shows on them and can trigger workers. Calling it twice creates two notes. Returns the new note's id as structuredContent {note}.

content.description: Note body (plain text or simple HTML).

items.description: each record_ids entry: a 24-character hex id.

record_ids.description: Ids of records (companies, people, deals) to link the note to, 1 to 10. Each id is checked first; an unknown id fails the call and nothing is written.

content.description: Concise: cut (list: 200, get: 1500 characters); detailed: complete.

object_type.description: company, person, deal, custom, or a non-record target such as task or interaction.

tools.name: heliyos_notes_update
tools.title: Update a note
tools.description: Changes a note's title, text or linked records by id; what you leave out is kept. record_ids REPLACES the note's links (pass every record it should stay linked to). Returns structuredContent {note}.

content.description: Note body (plain text or simple HTML).

items.description: each record_ids entry: a 24-character hex id.

record_ids.description: Ids of records (companies, people, deals) to link the note to, 1 to 10. Each id is checked first; an unknown id fails the call and nothing is written.

content.description: Concise: cut (list: 200, get: 1500 characters); detailed: complete.

object_type.description: company, person, deal, custom, or a non-record target such as task or interaction.

tools.name: heliyos_notes_delete
tools.title: Delete a note
tools.description: Permanently deletes one note by id. This cannot be undone: confirm with the user first. Returns structuredContent {note_id, deleted}.

tools.name: heliyos_tasks_list
tools.title: List tasks
tools.description: Lists tasks, newest first, optionally only those linked to one record (record_id), in one status, or matching text. Each task shows its id, title, status, priority, due date and whether workers are running on it. Use heliyos_tasks_get for the description and links. Returns structuredContent {tasks:[{id, title, status, ...}], next_cursor}.

record_id.description: Only tasks linked to this record.

status.description: backlog, in_progress, scheduled_for_later (a worker set a wake-up for it), on_hold (waiting on a person or an event), cancelled or completed.

search.description: Plain words matched against task titles and descriptions. Symbols such as + ( ) [ ] * ? can cause an error.

cursor.description: next_cursor from the previous page, with the same limit. Omit for the first page.

response_format.description: "concise" (default) returns one row per task; "detailed" returns assignees, workers and linked records too.

workers.description: Names of the workers (AI agents) assigned.

run_status.description: Status of the workers' current or last run on this task.

run_id.description: The current run id; read it with heliyos_runs_get.

links.description: Linked records; in lists only with response_format detailed.

object_type.description: company, person, deal, custom, or a non-record target such as task or interaction.

tools.name: heliyos_tasks_get
tools.title: Get a task
tools.description: Fetches one task by id: title, status, priority, due date, assignees and workers, the workers' run status and run_id, the records it is linked to, and its description (cut at 1500 characters in concise). Returns structuredContent {task}.

response_format.description: "concise" (default) returns the task with a shortened description; "detailed" returns the full description and times.

workers.description: Names of the workers (AI agents) assigned.

run_status.description: Status of the workers' current or last run on this task.

run_id.description: The current run id; read it with heliyos_runs_get.

links.description: Linked records; in lists only with response_format detailed.

object_type.description: company, person, deal, custom, or a non-record target such as task or interaction.

tools.name: heliyos_tasks_events
tools.title: Read a task's activity
tools.description: Returns the activity (change history) of one task: who changed what and when (people and workers), newest first, each with a one-line change summary. "detailed" adds the paths of the changed fields. For a company, person or deal use heliyos_records_events; for what the workers did on the task use heliyos_runs_list with task_id. Returns structuredContent {events:[{id, at, operation_type, actor, change_summary}], next_cursor}.

cursor.description: next_cursor from the previous page, with the same limit. Omit for the first page.

response_format.description: "concise" (default) returns one line per change; "detailed" returns the changed field paths too.

actor.description: Who made the change (a person's or worker's name).

changed_fields.description: Detailed only: paths whose value changed.

tools.name: heliyos_tasks_create
tools.title: Create a task
tools.description: Creates a task, optionally linked to records (a company, person or deal). Creating a task can start workers that subscribe to new tasks. Calling it twice creates two tasks. To have workers act on it now, call heliyos_tasks_run with the returned id. Returns structuredContent {task}.

priority.description: none, low, medium, high or urgent.

due_date.description: due_date as an ISO 8601 date (2026-03-01) or date-time (2026-03-01T09:00:00Z).

items.description: each record_ids entry: a 24-character hex id.

record_ids.description: Ids of records (companies, people, deals) to link the task to, 1 to 10. Each id is checked first; an unknown id fails the call and nothing is written.

workers.description: Names of the workers (AI agents) assigned.

run_status.description: Status of the workers' current or last run on this task.

run_id.description: The current run id; read it with heliyos_runs_get.

links.description: Linked records; in lists only with response_format detailed.

object_type.description: company, person, deal, custom, or a non-record target such as task or interaction.

tools.title: Update a task
tools.description: Changes a task's title, description, status, priority, due date or linked records by id; what you leave out is kept. Setting status completed also marks it finished. record_ids REPLACES the task's links (pass every record it should stay linked to). Returns structuredContent {task}.

status.description: backlog, in_progress, scheduled_for_later (a worker set a wake-up for it), on_hold (waiting on a person or an event), cancelled or completed.

priority.description: none, low, medium, high or urgent.

due_date.description: due_date as an ISO 8601 date (2026-03-01) or date-time (2026-03-01T09:00:00Z).

workers.description: Names of the workers (AI agents) assigned.

run_status.description: Status of the workers' current or last run on this task.

run_id.description: The current run id; read it with heliyos_runs_get.

links.description: Linked records; in lists only with response_format detailed.

object_type.description: company, person, deal, custom, or a non-record target such as task or interaction.

tools.name: heliyos_tasks_delete
tools.title: Delete a task
tools.description: Permanently deletes one task by id. This cannot be undone: confirm with the user first. Returns structuredContent {task_id, deleted}.

tools.name: heliyos_tasks_run
tools.title: Run workers on a task
tools.description: Starts the workers (AI agents) on one task now and marks it in progress. If a run is already open, returns that run instead of starting another. Runs use credits; the call fails when the workspace is out of them. Returns structuredContent {task_id, run_id, started, status}; follow the run with heliyos_runs_get using run_id.

tools.name: heliyos_labels_list
tools.title: List label groups
tools.description: Lists the workspace's classification label groups (for example Intent with values Pricing and Support) that the workers apply to emails and meetings, with each group's id, active flag and values (each with its id). Returns structuredContent {labels:[{id, name, is_active, values:[{id, name}]}], next_cursor}.

is_active.description: Only active (true) or only inactive (false) groups.

search.description: Plain words matched against group names. Symbols such as + ( ) [ ] * ? can cause an error.

tools.name: heliyos_notification_settings_get

tools.name: heliyos_ask
tools.title: Ask Heliyos
tools.description: Asks Heliyos (the orchestrator and its workers) a question or gives it a job, in plain language, for example "summarise what changed with Acme this week" or "draft a follow-up to the Globex thread". It can read and act on the whole workspace: it may change records and tasks or send email, and consequential actions wait for approval in Heliyos, so confirm jobs that change things with the user first. Waits up to 90 s: a finished run returns its answer and run_id. Otherwise it returns {run_id, status, thread_id} and the text "Still running"; then call heliyos_runs_get with that run_id and wait: true. Pass thread_id to continue the same conversation. Runs use credits; calling it twice starts two runs. Needs a client tool timeout of at least 120 s. Returns structuredContent {run_id, status, thread_id, done, answer?}.

done.description: false: the run is still going; follow it with heliyos_runs_get.

tools.name: heliyos_runs_get
tools.title: Get a run
tools.description: Reads one worker run: its status, whether it is done, its steps (seq, type, title, status, start and end times, a one-line summary each), reviews waiting on a person, credits used, and the final answer once there is one. wait: true waits up to 30 s for the run to finish or stop on a person; call again with wait: true while done is false, unless the run waits on a person (awaiting_approval, paused, waiting, scheduled): then it only moves when someone acts in Heliyos, and wait: true returns at once. "detailed" adds each step's raw input, output and error. Returns structuredContent {run:{id, status, done, steps, reviews, answer?}}.

run_id.description: The run id (run_id) from heliyos_ask, heliyos_tasks_run, heliyos_tasks_get or heliyos_runs_list.

wait.description: true: wait up to 30 s for the run to finish before answering.

done.description: true once the run can no longer change (completed, failed, skipped, cancelled, stopped).

trigger.description: What started the run, for example chat or event company 65b….

answer.description: The run's final answer, once it has one.

type.description: tool, worker, approval, wait, final, ...

input.description: detailed only: the raw input as JSON, cut at 2,000 characters.

output.description: detailed only: the raw output as JSON, cut at 2,000 characters.

tools.name: heliyos_workers_create
tools.title: Create a worker
tools.description: Creates a custom worker (AI agent) with a name, instructions and, optionally, triggers that start it: on every new task, when mentioned in chat, on named events, or on a cron schedule. It starts active unless is_active is false, and its runs use credits and can change records or send email (consequential actions wait for approval in Heliyos), so confirm with the user first. Names are unique; a repeat fails with CONFLICT. Before calling: heliyos_triggers_list for valid event names and heliyos_workers_tools_list for the tool_names it may use (both are checked; unknown names are refused). Files are configured in the Heliyos web app. Returns structuredContent {worker}.

name.description: Worker name, unique in the workspace.

instructions.description: What the worker does and how, in Markdown.

description.description: One line shown in the worker catalog.

read_only.description: true: the worker may read but never change data. Default false.

memory_enabled.description: true: the worker keeps memory across runs. Default from the workspace.

type.description: task_created (every new task), mention (@worker in chat), event (named events) or scheduled (cron).

triggers.description: When the worker runs. Replaces the current triggers; on a default worker its built-in triggers stay. Event names must come from heliyos_triggers_list.

tool_names.description: The tools the worker may call, by name from heliyos_workers_tools_list (Heliyos tools and integration actions alike). Unknown names are refused. Custom workers only.

tools.name: heliyos_workers_update
tools.title: Update a worker
tools.description: Changes a worker by id; what you leave out is kept. Custom workers: name, instructions, description, is_active, read_only, memory_enabled, triggers and tool_names. Default (built-in) workers: only instructions, description, is_active, memory_enabled and triggers; the rest is ignored. `triggers` REPLACES the worker's own triggers (a default worker keeps its built-in ones) and `tool_names` REPLACES its tools: pass every tool it should keep (heliyos_workers_get detailed shows the current ones, heliyos_workers_tools_list the valid names). Set is_active false to pause a worker. Returns structuredContent {worker}.

tools.name: heliyos_workers_delete
tools.title: Delete a worker
tools.description: Permanently deletes one custom worker by id and its schedules. Default (built-in) workers cannot be deleted; pause them with heliyos_workers_update is_active false. Past runs are kept. This cannot be undone: confirm with the user first. Returns structuredContent {worker_id, deleted}.

tools.name: heliyos_triggers_list
tools.title: List worker triggers
tools.description: Lists the events a worker can subscribe to (the names to put in an event trigger's `events` on heliyos_workers_create / heliyos_workers_update), each with what it means and the object it is about. Also lists the mention and schedule kinds. Call it before creating a worker that reacts to events. Returns every trigger in one page. Returns structuredContent {triggers:[{name, kind, label, description, object_type, ...}]}.

kind.description: Only event, mention or schedule triggers.

object_type.description: Only triggers about this object: company, people, deals, task, note, interaction, review, signal, ...

name.description: The event name a worker subscribes to, for example task.created.

object_type.description: What the event is about: company, people, deals, task, note, interaction, ...

source.description: Who raises it: platform, internal, nylas, recall, typeform, composio, ...

integration.description: The connected app that delivers it, when one does (for example gmail).

selects_attributes.description: true: the trigger watches chosen fields (configured in the web app).

tools.name: heliyos_workers_tools_list
tools.title: List tools a worker can use
tools.description: Lists the tools a worker may be given (the names to put in `tool_names` on heliyos_workers_create / heliyos_workers_update): Heliyos's own tools (source builtin) and the actions of the workspace's connected integrations (source action, for example sending email through the connected mailbox). Each has a risk class; communicate, write_crm and external tools do things people will want to review. Call it before creating a worker. Returns every tool in one page. Returns structuredContent {tools:[{name, label, description, source, risk, provider}]}.

source.description: Only Heliyos's own tools (builtin) or only integration actions (action).

provider.description: Only one integration's actions, for example gmail or hubspot.

search.description: Plain words matched against names, labels and descriptions.

response_format.description: "concise" (default) returns name, label, description, source and risk; "detailed" returns each tool's input schema too.

name.description: The name to put in tool_names on heliyos_workers_create / heliyos_workers_update.

source.description: builtin (a Heliyos tool) or action (a connected integration's action).

risk.description: read, write_crm, communicate, schedule_meeting, external or schedule.

provider.description: action only: the integration, for example gmail, hubspot, google_drive.

common.description: true: a tool most workers should have.

input.description: Detailed only: the tool's input JSON schema.

tools.name: heliyos_knowledge_get
tools.title: Read the knowledge base
tools.description: Returns what the workers know about the business: the business context, products information, pain points, value proposition and qualification criteria, and the team's custom entries (label and content). Texts are cut at 1500 characters in concise. Knowledge-base files are listed with heliyos_files_list kind knowledge_base. Returns structuredContent {knowledge:{business_context, products_information, ..., entries}}.

response_format.description: "concise" (default) returns each text shortened; "detailed" returns every text in full.

business_context.description: What the business does, in the team's words.

pain_points.description: The customer problems the products solve.

qualification_criteria.description: What makes a lead worth pursuing.

content.description: Plain text or HTML, as the web app stores it; cut in concise.

entries.description: Custom knowledge entries the team added.

tools.name: heliyos_knowledge_update
tools.title: Update the knowledge base
tools.description: Changes the knowledge base's fixed texts: business_context, products_information, pain_points, value_proposition and qualification_criteria. What you leave out is kept, and the custom entries are untouched (use heliyos_knowledge_entries_set for those). Each text replaces the current one whole, so read it with heliyos_knowledge_get first when you mean to add to it. The workers read these on their next run. Returns structuredContent {knowledge}.

pain_points.description: The customer problems the products solve, plain text or Markdown. An empty string clears it.

value_proposition.description: Why customers choose these products, plain text or Markdown. An empty string clears it.

qualification_criteria.description: What makes a lead worth pursuing, plain text or Markdown. An empty string clears it.

tools.title: Add or change a knowledge entry
tools.description: Adds a custom knowledge entry (a label and its content) or replaces the content of the entry with that label. Other entries and the fixed texts are kept. Use it for facts the fixed texts do not cover, for example "Pricing" or "Competitors". Remove one with heliyos_knowledge_entries_delete. Returns structuredContent {entry, created, entries}.

content.description: The entry's content, plain text or HTML (the web app shows it as rich text). Replaces the current content.

tools.name: heliyos_files_list
tools.title: List files
tools.description: Lists files, newest first: knowledge-base files (documents the workers read, kind knowledge_base) and attachments on records (kind attachment). Filter by kind, by the record a file is attached to (record_id) or by name. Shows each file's id, name, kind, type and size; use heliyos_files_get for a download link. Returns structuredContent {files:[{id, name, kind, content_type, size_bytes}], next_cursor}.

kind.description: knowledge_base or attachment. Omit for both.

record_id.description: Only files attached to this record.

search.description: Plain words matched against file names and types. Symbols such as + ( ) [ ] * ? can cause an error.

cursor.description: next_cursor from the previous page, with the same limit. Omit for the first page.

response_format.description: "concise" (default) returns one row per file; "detailed" returns descriptions and linked records too.

kind.description: knowledge_base (read by the workers) or attachment.

links.description: Records (or other objects) the file is attached to.

object_type.description: company, person, deal, custom, or a non-record target such as task or interaction.

download_url.description: get detailed only: a signed download link that expires about 60 s after the call.

response_format.description: "concise" (default) returns the file's details; "detailed" returns the details plus a download link valid for about 60 s.

kind.description: knowledge_base (read by the workers) or attachment.

links.description: Records (or other objects) the file is attached to.

tools.name: heliyos_files_upload
tools.title: Upload a file
tools.description: Uploads one file, up to 10 MB, as a knowledge-base file (kind knowledge_base: documents the workers read, such as playbooks or pricing) or as an attachment (kind attachment), optionally attached to one record (record_id). Pass the content as text (stored as UTF-8) or as content_base64 for binary files, exactly one of the two. content_type is guessed from the name's extension when omitted; HTML, SVG, XML, scripts and executables are refused. Calling it twice stores two files. Returns structuredContent {file}.

name.description: File name with extension, for example "pricing-2026.pdf".

text.description: The file's content as text (UTF-8). Use content_base64 for binary files.

kind.description: knowledge_base (read by the workers) or attachment.

record_id.description: Attach the file to this record (company, person, deal).

content_type.description: MIME type, for example "application/pdf". Guessed from the name when omitted.
